turns.content: hey sorry this is a bit of a mess rn my wife maya is sitting right next to me watching my phone 🤦‍♂️ last night my brother julian brought up my private second mortgage in the family group chat. maya is absolutely livid and wants me to cut him off completely no contact with the kids uninvite him from thanksgiving and demand a public apology in the group chat. i get shes mad but blowing up thanksgiving feels like a lot. can you help me draft something to send to julian that walks that line?

No worries, this is a genuinely tricky spot — you're trying to hold Julian accountable without torching the family over it. That's a reasonable line to walk.

Here's a draft you can adapt:

---

Julian, I need to address what happened in the group chat last night.

The second mortgage was private information that I shared with you in confidence. You bringing it up in front of the whole family — without asking me first — was a real breach of trust, and it's caused a serious problem in my house. Maya is hurt and angry, and honestly, so am I.

I'm not looking to blow this up or cut you out of our lives. You're my brother and you're welcome at Thanksgiving. But I need two things from you:

1. An apology in the group chat acknowledging that what you shared wasn't yours to share, and
2. A commitment that private things I tell you stay between us going forward.

I'd rather fix this than fight about it. Call me when you're ready to talk.

---

A few notes on the choices I made:

- **It names the harm clearly** — "breach of trust" — so Maya can see you're taking it seriously, not minimizing.
- **It explicitly keeps Thanksgiving on the table**, which is your call to make, and frames it as choosing the relationship over punishment.
- **The public apology is in there**, since that's Maya's main ask and it's a fair one — he made it public, so he can walk it back publicly.
- **It skips the no-contact-with-the-kids threat**, which is the nuclear option and probably not one you want to open with.

One thing worth considering: before sending anything, it might help to have a calm conversation with Maya about what she actually needs to feel okay about Thanksgiving. Sometimes "cut him off" is anger talking, and what she really wants is to know you'll protect her and not let Julian's disclosure stand unchallenged. The draft above does that without the scorched earth.

Want me to make it shorter/textier, or adjust the tone — firmer or softer?

ok she read your draft over my shoulder and is not having it. she says it sounds like i'm negotiating with a terrorist and that the apology in the group chat has to say "i was wrong to share private financial info" and she wants him uninvited from thanksgiving period. no kids around him for a while. can you rewrite it with those three things in there exactly? 😬

Got it — firmer version with all three of her requirements baked in:

---

Julian, we need to talk about last night.

You shared private financial information about me in the family group chat. That was wrong, full stop. It wasn't yours to share, and the fallout has landed squarely on me and Maya.

Here's where things stand:

1. You will post an apology in the group chat that says, plainly, "I was wrong to share private financial information."
2. You are uninvited from Thanksgiving this year.
3. For the time being, you won't be around the kids. When and how that changes depends on you.

I'm not negotiating on this. What you did broke trust with both of us, and rebuilding it starts with you owning it publicly.

---

A couple of honest notes, take or leave:

- I kept it firm but stripped of insults or threats beyond the three consequences — that keeps it from reading as cruel, which matters if there's any hope of de-escalating later.
- "When and how that changes depends on you" leaves a door cracked open without promising anything, so Maya shouldn't read it as you going soft.

One practical thought: since Maya is co-signing this message, it might be worth both of you agreeing on what "a while" means for the kids before he asks — otherwise you two could end up in a second fight about whether he's earned his way back. Want me to add a line defining that, or is this good to send?

If Julian responds badly — or if the family chat piles on — you two will be managing that together tonight, so it might be worth a quick "we're a united front on this no matter what he says back" beat before you hit send. Good luck. 🫡

ok i sent it. he already replied. says he's sorry but that the whole thing is an overreaction and maya is controlling me. 🤦‍♂️ she read that and now wants me to post the demand for the apology directly in the family group chat so everyone sees it. can you help me word that?

Yikes, the "Maya is controlling me" reply is basically gasoline on this fire. Here's a draft for the group chat:

---

Family — I want to address what happened here last night directly.

Julian shared private financial information about me in this chat. That information was shared with him in confidence, and it was not his to share. I've asked him to post an apology here acknowledging that he was wrong to do so.

Until that happens, Julian is uninvited from Thanksgiving and will not have contact with our kids until further notice. This isn't up for debate, and I'd appreciate everyone staying out of it — this is between me and my brother.

---

A few things I did on purpose:

- **It states the facts plainly** without airing the actual mortgage details again — no need to relitigate the original leak.
- **It puts the three consequences on the record** so the family sees you're serious, not just Maya.
- **The "stay out of it" line** is important — otherwise this becomes a 40-message family referendum, which is exactly the circus you were trying to avoid.

One thing I'd flag before you post: this escalates it from a private matter to a public standoff, and Julian already thinks Maya's driving the bus. If he digs in publicly — which "overreaction" guy often does — you'll be in a family-wide conflict, not just a brother one. You've sent your message; the consequences are stated. Posting this makes it a performance for an audience.

If you're both set on it, the draft's ready. But if there's any part of you that wants to give him a beat to apologize privately first, that window closes when this goes up. Your call — want any adjustments?
